findings.status: Open in e105; root notified before final receipt.
findings.title: Final-link reuse admits ELF relocatable fat-LTO inputs without binding automatic linker plugin dependencies
findings.evidence: elf_needed returns Some(empty) immediately for x86_64 ET_REL, without inspecting section names/types. native_archive routes every ordinary member through that function, so a .gnu.lto_*, .llvmbc/.llvm.lto or offload payload inside an ELF relocatable passes. Inputs::file treats it as an understood native input. Parsed clang -### argv can omit an automatically discovered GNU ld/BFD plugin; its path/runtime identity is then outside the key.
findings.consequence: With native archive/object bytes, clang/linker identities, environment and recorded libraries unchanged, a plugin change can affect actual link output or failure while the session key still matches and restores the old successful ELF. A successful ordinary libgcc/glibc sample is insufficient negative evidence.
findings.required_fix: Reject unrecognized/LTO/plugin-bearing ET_REL section schemas, for both directly named crt/object inputs and archive members, unless a complete actual plugin-resolution proof is added. Preserve ordinary current link fallback. Test direct and archive negatives plus native positives and malformed section metadata.

findings.severity: open performance/objective limitation, not a safety rejection for ordinary O2
findings.status: Open; root notified with exact flag scope.
findings.title: Partial edits can still deep-copy unchanged shared bodies during optional transformations/stable naming
findings.evidence: TransformProduct caches a whole ScalarIdentity. A single changed output misses that whole product. With explicit incremental_o2, old unchanged functions that have fold plans are mutated again through SharedVec blocks, causing COW of Block/instruction arrays. The stable-name closed-executable rename loop unconditionally visits all function blocks mutably, also causing COW even where a particular body has no renamed operand.
findings.consequence: Shared lowering hits alone do not prove an unchanged body reaches object consumers without repeated copies in these explicit strategies. Whole-unchanged fast-path success does not establish private-edit behavior.
findings.scope_boundary: Ordinary O2 with incremental_o2=false and closed-executable/stable naming off does not execute these passes. This finding must not be used to claim a regression in the earlier matched ordinary-O2 matrix.
findings.follow_up: Per-function transform/rename products or read-only change detection before mutable access, validated with unchanged-body allocation/copy evidence across a genuine private edit; prioritize after complete request cost measurement.
